item.title: CVE-2026-97024 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
A path traversal vulnerability in Flatpak's handling of the files/etc directory during app deployment allows a malicious Flatpak app to cause certain host system files (such as passwd, group, machine-id, or resolv.conf) to be emptied or replaced with a symlink when the app is installed or upgraded. In system-wide installations, the write is performed as root.
Score: 7.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-96541 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
A denial-of-service flaw was found in gnome-remote-desktop. An unauthenticated remote attacker can open RDP connections without completing the handshake and retain the connection-throttling slots indefinitely because no pre-authentication handshake deadline is enforced. By exhausting the global connection limit, an attacker can prevent new RDP clients from connecting until a holding socket is closed.
Score: 7.5 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-96295
item.description:
Authenticated users can bypass normal controls on the reading and writing of workflow execution results. This allows any authenticated user to read or modify any other user's workflow execution results.
This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

item.title: CVE-2026-84838 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
A flaw was found in rpmuncompress. This command injection vulnerability allows a local attacker to execute arbitrary commands. This occurs when rpmuncompress processes a specially crafted archive filename containing shell metacharacters, which are not properly escaped before being passed to shell command strings. Successful exploitation requires user interaction, where a user or automated workflow invokes rpmuncompress on the malicious file, leading to high impact on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data accessible to the invoking user.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-84837 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
A flaw was found in rpm. An attacker can exploit a command injection vulnerability by influencing the path or filename of a tarball processed by `rpmbuild -t*` to include shell metacharacters. This is particularly relevant in automated build or continuous integration (CI) workflows that ingest externally supplied artifact names. Successful exploitation allows for arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the build user, which could lead to information disclosure or disruption of the build environment.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-84233 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
A flaw was found in rpm. A local attacker could supply a specially crafted `.gem` filename containing RPM macro syntax. When a user or automated workflow invokes `rpmuncompress -x` on this file, the macro expansion occurs during command construction. This allows the attacker to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the invoking account, leading to a compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
Score: 7 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-79655 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
A flaw was found in sos clean, a utility within the sos package. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to perform arbitrary file creation or overwrite. By crafting a malicious tar archive, an attacker can exploit a path traversal issue during tar extraction, where symlink and hardlink targets are not properly validated. This enables the attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the system with the privileges of the sos clean process, which often runs as root.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-78367 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).
Score: 7 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-133667 [CVSS:4.0 4.8 MEDIUM]
item.description:
flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users.
- Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser.
- Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced <mark> elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting.
- Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context.
Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints.
Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity.
Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133665 [CVSS:4.0 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
flowintel contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to access sensitive configuration data and logs intended for administrators only.
The notification page and alert API responses exposed sensitive fields, including webhook URLs, signing secrets, IMAP credentials, and delivery logs, in the initial data or JSON responses. Although the user interface hid the configuration form from non-admin users, the underlying data remained accessible via the page source or API endpoints. This exposure included historical webhook URLs that may contain active bearer tokens.
An attacker with a valid non-admin account could retrieve these credentials and logs, potentially leading to unauthorized access to notification services, impersonation of the application in webhook deliveries, or further lateral movement within the infrastructure.
Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133663 [CVSS:4.0 8.6 HIGH]
item.description:
flowintel contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability affecting multiple endpoints that manage child records of cases and tasks. An authenticated user with access to one case or task could read or modify records belonging to other cases by supplying identifiers of those records directly in the request.
Affected operations include: - Reading task notes, subtasks, and URL tools by referencing their IDs without verifying they belong to the authorized task - Retrieving task assignees for a task belonging to a different case - Editing or deleting timeline events and timeline event links belonging to another case - Editing or removing case connectors belonging to another case - Invoking connector module operations (MISP, generic connectors, worker calls) by combining an authorized case with a connector link from a different case
The root cause is that the application authorized the parent resource (case or task) in the URL but then fetched or operated on the child record independently without verifying the child's ownership relationship to the authorized parent.
Security impact: an authenticated user can exfiltrate sensitive threat intelligence data from cases they do not have access to, and can modify or delete timeline entries, connector configurations, and other records in unauthorized cases, leading to data integrity loss and potential disruption of incident response workflows.
Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133662 [CVSS:4.0 8.4 HIGH]
item.description:
flowintel contains multiple authorization bypass vulnerabilities in its Analyzer (MISP Modules) functionality, affecting both the web interface and the REST API.
- Saving analyzer results to a case or task accepted caller-supplied case and task identifiers without verifying that the authenticated user is a member of the target case or holds the required restricted-task permissions. An authenticated user could write notes, create tasks, and attach MISP objects or attributes into another organization's case.
- Stored analyzer results were retrievable by UUID by any authenticated user. Both the web endpoint and the API endpoint returned the full result payload without checking ownership, exposing another user's analysis output.
- The save handler did not validate the structure of the request, did not reject conflicting destination selections, and did not halt processing when a task-note operation failed, allowing partial or unintended writes.
Preconditions: the attacker must possess a valid authenticated session (or API token) in flowintel. No administrative role is required.
Security impact: unauthorized cross-tenant data disclosure (analyzer results) and unauthorized cross-tenant data modification (notes, tasks, MISP objects/attributes in another organization's case).
Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133661 [CVSS:4.0 5.3 MEDIUM]
item.description:
FlowIntel contains multiple authorization and credential management vulnerabilities affecting connector instances, MISP helper tools, and case templates.
- Connector instance metadata, connectivity checks, and case listings accepted instance IDs without verifying if the acting user had visibility or ownership rights, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive configuration and data. - Case template serialization and creation processes exposed connector instances attached to templates regardless of the user's permissions, potentially leaking credentials or instance details to users who should not have access. - Editing connector instances allowed changes to URLs or sharing scopes without requiring re-authentication of API keys, enabling the reuse of another user's credentials in a new context or the leakage of shared keys to unauthorized endpoints. - Outbound MISP connector keys were incorrectly accepted for authenticating incoming alerts, bypassing the intended separation between outbound integration credentials and inbound alert source authentication.
These issues allow authenticated users to access unauthorized connector data, manipulate credential scopes, and potentially exploit credential confusion between different security contexts.
Affected versions: < 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133660 [CVSS:4.0 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its user directory and assignment endpoints that allows authenticated users to access data belonging to other organisations.
When the LIMIT_USER_VIEW_TO_ORG setting is enabled to restrict directory visibility to the caller's organisation, several API endpoints (user lookup by ID, last name, Matrix ID, and role-based listings) did not consistently enforce the organisation boundary. An authenticated non-admin user could retrieve profiles of users in other organisations by supplying their identifiers.
Additionally, OrgAdmin users could retrieve the task assignments of any user in the system, including tasks and case titles from private cases to which they had no access. The assignment endpoints did not verify that the requested user belonged to the caller's organisation or that the underlying cases were visible to the caller.
Security impact: - Exposure of user identities (names, Matrix IDs, roles) across organisation boundaries - Disclosure of task assignments, case titles, and workflow details from private cases - Potential enumeration of other organisations' membership and case activity
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133659 [CVSS:4.0 8.6 HIGH]
item.description:
Flowintel contains multiple SSO identity and organisation trust boundary violations that collectively allow account takeover, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access to private case data.
- Keycloak SSO accepted unverified email claims, and all SSO providers (Keycloak, Entra ID, SimpleSAML) could resolve a claimed email address to an existing account that was created via a different sign-in method, enabling cross-provider account collision and unauthorized access to another user's account and data.
- Entra ID role mapping relied on group display names, which tenant members could duplicate by creating a group with the same name as a privileged group (e.g. FlowintelAdmin), resulting in unauthorized role escalation.
- SSO provisioning reused organisations whose display names matched user-controlled profile names, granting the new SSO user access to that organisation's private cases without explicit administrator assignment.
- Case sharing via the API resolved organisations by name using a first-match query, so ambiguous names could silently resolve to the wrong organisation.
Preconditions: an attacker must have a valid SSO identity (Keycloak, Entra ID, or SimpleSAML) or be a member of the relevant Entra tenant. No local administrator access is required.
Security impact: unauthorized access to private case data, privilege escalation to Editor or higher roles, and account takeover across authentication providers.
Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
Score: 8.6 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X

item.title: CVE-2026-133658 [CVSS:4.0 6.3 MEDIUM]
item.description:
Flowintel contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in its Matrix relay (bot) integration. When the relay forwarded API requests on behalf of a represented user, the authorization and permission checks evaluated the relay bot's elevated role while the request handlers acted as the lower-privileged represented user. This mismatch allowed users with restricted roles (e.g., Read Only) to perform write operations, directory lookups, calendar modifications, assignment changes, template creation, and import actions they were not authorized to perform.
Additionally, relay authority was determined by matching editable user profile fields (name and email) rather than a protected, non-spoofable identifier. An ordinary user who modified their profile to match the expected bot name could be recognized as the trusted relay, enabling impersonation of the bot and potential access to its elevated privileges.
Preconditions: - A valid Flowintel user account with a restricted role (e.g., Read Only) - Access to the Matrix relay integration or the ability to send API requests with the relay's API key and a MATRIX-ID header - For the impersonation vector: ability to edit one's own profile name fields
Security impact: - Unauthorized write operations by users with read-only or otherwise restricted permissions - Potential impersonation of the trusted relay bot by ordinary users - Bypass of organization-level access controls and role-based restrictions - Unauthorized modification of cases, tasks, calendar events, templates, and user directory entries
Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133652 [CVSS:4.0 7.2 HIGH]
item.description:
Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. The session identifier used a bare numeric user ID rather than a credential-bound token, resulting in several related weaknesses:
- Remembered logins (remember-me cookies) remained valid after a user changed their password, allowing an attacker holding a previously issued cookie to retain access indefinitely. - Server-side session identifiers were not rotated upon login (local, SSO, or remembered), enabling session fixation. - Self-service email and password changes did not require verification of the current password, permitting an attacker with an active session to modify account credentials without knowledge of the existing password. - Administrator-initiated password resets did not revoke other browser sessions, invalidate remembered logins, or rotate the affected user's API key.
An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. Additionally, an attacker with any valid session could change the account's email address or password without knowing the current credentials, effectively taking over the account.
Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133651 [CVSS:4.0 6.1 MEDIUM]
item.description:
FlowIntel contained a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability affecting fourteen web routes that performed destructive or state-changing operations. The affected routes accepted HTTP GET requests in addition to (or instead of) POST, which bypassed the Flask-WTF CSRF token validation that is only enforced on non-GET requests.
The vulnerable operations included: - Case deletion and case merging - Organisation removal from a case - Task deletion (case and template) - Case template and note template deletion - Connector, connector instance, and icon deletion - Custom tag deletion and status change - Taxonomy and galaxy status changes
An attacker who could induce an authenticated user to follow a crafted link or load a page containing a cross-site navigation (e.g., an image tag or redirect) could trigger any of these destructive actions using the victim's session cookie, without the victim's explicit consent or awareness. No special privileges beyond a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role (editor or admin) were required on the victim's account.
Security impact: unauthorized deletion or modification of cases, tasks, templates, connectors, icons, custom tags, taxonomies, and galaxies belonging to the victim or the organisation, resulting in loss of data integrity.
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133648 [CVSS:4.0 9.9 CRITICAL]
item.description:
Flowintel disabled TLS certificate verification for all MISP API connections and used unverified SSL contexts for IMAP and SMTP STARTTLS mail connections. This allowed an on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacker positioned between Flowintel and its MISP or mail servers to impersonate the remote server and intercept sensitive data.
Affected connections include: - All MISP HTTPS API calls (event retrieval, attribute search, event creation, connectivity checks, and API validation) - SMTP STARTTLS connections used for sending email notifications - IMAP TLS connections used for fetching mail archives and testing connectivity
An attacker who can observe or intercept network traffic between Flowintel and the MISP or mail server could: - Capture MISP API keys and mail credentials (SMTP/IMAP passwords) - Read all threat intelligence data exchanged (events, attributes, objects, reports) - Inject or modify threat intelligence data returned to Flowintel
The vulnerability required no authentication on the part of the attacker and no user interaction; it was exploitable by any party with a network position between Flowintel and its configured MISP or mail endpoints.
Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-53431 [CVSS:4.0 9.1 CRITICAL]
item.description:
Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in malach-it Boruta allows an attacker who has obtained a previously valid JWT client assertion to authenticate as the issuing OAuth client after the assertion has expired.
Boruta accepts JWT-based client authentication (client_secret_jwt and private_key_jwt token endpoint authentication methods) but never enforces that the assertion's exp claim is in the future. The pre-check helper Boruta.Oauth.Request.Base.check_expiration/1 in lib/boruta/oauth/request/base.ex only verifies that an exp claim is present (it pattern-matches on the existence of the key and returns success), and the Joken token configuration used for signature verification, Boruta.Oauth.Authorization.Client.Token.token_config/0 in lib/boruta/oauth/authorization/client.ex, returns an empty map, so Joken's default exp claim validator is not engaged either. Any attacker who obtains a validly-signed client assertion (for example through logs, reverse proxies, browser tooling, or other observability surfaces) can replay it indefinitely to authenticate as the client and obtain access tokens with that client's privileges.
This issue affects boruta: from 2.3.0 before 2.3.7 and from 3.0.0-beta.1 onward.

item.title: CVE-2026-53430 [CVSS:4.0 8.7 HIGH]
item.description:
Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc (GRPC.Compressor.Gzip, GRPC.Message modules) allows a denial of service via a gzip decompression bomb.
This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/grpc/compressor/gzip.ex, lib/grpc/message.ex and program routines GRPC.Compressor.Gzip.decompress/1, GRPC.Message.from_data/2.
GRPC.Compressor.Gzip.decompress/1 calls :zlib.gunzip/1 directly on attacker-controlled bytes with no decompressed-size limit, ratio check, or incremental decoding. Because this module is the registered gzip GRPC.Compressor implementation, it is invoked automatically whenever an incoming gRPC frame carries the grpc-encoding: gzip header. :zlib.gunzip/1 allocates the entire decompressed result as a single binary, so a small highly compressible payload (for example a few kilobytes of zeros, which gzip compresses at roughly 1000:1) expands to multiple gigabytes inside a single call. The max_receive_message_length limit is enforced only against the already-decompressed message, so it provides no protection. An unauthenticated remote peer can send a single crafted frame to exhaust the BEAM node's heap and trigger an out-of-memory kill.
This issue affects grpc: from 0.4.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_core: from 1.0.0-alfa before 1.0.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133631 [CVSS:4.0 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:

An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints.
- AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user.
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-121481 [CVSS:3.1 9.8 CRITICAL]
item.description:
Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.
Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.
CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a heap buffer overflow in the calling process.
Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.
The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the defect can be reached.
FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
Score: 9.8 (CRITICAL) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

On the v1 line the lookup also falls back to a class-and-key-type-only search when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, pairing a label-only private key with the first public key of its type on the token.
The v1 module paths are deprecated and will not be fixed; users should migrate to github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 version 2.0.0-rc9 or later.

item.title: CVE-2026-53429 [CVSS:4.0 6.9 MEDIUM]
item.description:
Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in leandrocp mdex and mdex_native allows an attacker who controls a rendered document to cause a denial of service through unbounded native memory exhaustion.
The native rendering code permanently leaks memory when rendering a document that contains escaped-tag nodes. The conversion of each %MDEx.EscapedTag{} node into its native representation (From<ExEscapedTag> for NodeValue in the Rust NIF) calls Box::leak on the caller-supplied literal string, which surrenders the backing allocation so that it lives for the entire lifetime of the operating system process and is never freed.
Both the byte length of each literal and the number of escaped-tag nodes in a document are attacker-controlled, and there is no size cap, rate limit, or string interning on this path. Every render of a document containing escaped-tag nodes therefore leaks literal_size × node_count bytes that can never be reclaimed, and repeated renders accumulate without bound. Rendering reaches this path through the public MDEx.to_html/1 entry point and any other API that renders a supplied %MDEx.Document{}.
Any application that uses mdex (or mdex_native directly) to render documents derived from user-supplied content is affected. Because the leaked memory is never reclaimed for the life of the BEAM process, an attacker can drive resident memory upward without limit until the node exhausts memory and crashes, taking down every process on it.
The vulnerable native code originally shipped inside mdex (in native/comrak_nif/src/types/document.rs) and was later extracted into the separate mdex_native package (native/mdex_native_nif/src/types/document.rs).
This issue affects mdex: from 0.11.1 before 0.12.3; mdex_native: from 0.1.0 before 0.2.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-53428 [CVSS:4.0 6.9 MEDIUM]
item.description:
Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value vulnerability in leandrocp mdex allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service through unbounded memory allocation.
comrak_nif::lumis_adapter::LumisAdapter::parse_highlight_lines in native/comrak_nif/src/lumis_adapter.rs eagerly expands a user-controlled inclusive line range from a fenced code block's highlight_lines decorator into a Vec<usize>, pushing one element per integer in the range with no upper bound on the range size. A payload that differs by only a few bytes can therefore allocate hundreds of megabytes, and a sufficiently large range (for example 1-2000000000) exhausts host memory and aborts the BEAM, denying service to every user of the rendering process. The per-line write loop additionally tests membership with a linear scan over the same vector, degrading rendering to a quadratic cost even for ranges that do not immediately exhaust memory.
The vulnerable native code originally shipped inside mdex (in native/comrak_nif/src/autumnus_adapter.rs, later renamed to native/comrak_nif/src/lumis_adapter.rs) and was later extracted into the separate mdex_native package (native/mdex_native_nif/src/lumis_adapter.rs).

item.title: CVE-2026-53427 [CVSS:4.0 2.3 LOW]
item.description:
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in leandrocp MDEx allows stored or reflected cross-site scripting via attacker-controlled Markdown.
When syntax highlighting and full info-string forwarding (render: [full_info_string: true]) are enabled, the Lumis adapter copies the value of a code fence's highlight_lines_class info-string attribute, unescaped, into the class attribute of every rendered line. comrak_nif::lumis_adapter::LumisAdapter::parse_custom_attributes in native/comrak_nif/src/lumis_adapter.rs shlex-parses the info string and stores each key=value pair verbatim, highlight_lines_config pulls highlight_lines_class into the per-line class value, and write_highlighted interpolates that value directly into the class attribute of the per-line <div>. item.title: CVE-2026-53426 [CVSS:4.0 8.2 HIGH]
item.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in leandrocp MDEx allows Excessive Allocation.
MDEx.parse_document/2 accepts a {:json, json} source. In lib/mdex.ex, the private json_to_node/1 function passes the attacker-controlled node_type value to Module.concat/1, which calls String.to_atom/1 and interns a brand-new atom for every distinct value. Atoms are never garbage collected on the BEAM, so a crafted JSON document carrying a unique node_type at each (deeply nested) node mints one permanent atom per node.
A single document can intern hundreds of thousands of atoms, and a large enough document exhausts the default atom table (around 1,048,576 atoms) and aborts the entire Erlang VM, taking down every process on the node. Any application that passes untrusted input to the {:json, ...} source of MDEx.parse_document is exposed to an unauthenticated denial-of-service.
This issue affects mdex: from 0.4.3 before 0.13.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-49757 [CVSS:4.0 9.2 CRITICAL]
item.description:
Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability in team-alembic AshAuthentication allows account takeover of local users via OAuth2/OIDC sign-in.
AshAuthentication's OAuth2 and OIDC family strategies matched the local user by email address (an upsert on the email field, or a user-defined sign-in filter) rather than by the OpenID Connect iss/sub claim combination. An unauthenticated attacker who can register an account on any accepted OAuth provider with the victim's email (or who benefits from provider-side email reuse or reclamation) obtains the victim's full local privileges.
The fix resolves users by the (strategy, sub) identity stored in a user identity resource, and only links a new sub to an existing local account by email when the provider's email_verified claim is trusted (trust_email_verified?).

item.description:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in wojtekmach Req allows multipart parameter smuggling via attacker-influenced part metadata.

Any application that forwards user-controlled filenames (or field names / MIME types) through Req.post/2 with form_multipart: lets an attacker inject arbitrary headers into the outgoing multipart body or smuggle additional fields and parts into the request the victim service sends downstream.

item.title: CVE-2026-49755 [CVSS:4.0 8.2 HIGH]
item.description:
Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in wojtekmach Req allows attacker-controlled HTTP servers to exhaust memory in a Req client via decompression-bomb response bodies.
Req's default response pipeline includes Req.Steps.decode_body/1 and Req.Steps.decompress_body/1 in lib/req/steps.ex. decode_body/1 dispatches on the server-supplied content-type (or URL extension) and calls :zip.extract(body, [:memory]) for application/zip, :erl_tar.extract({:binary, body}, [:memory]) for application/x-tar, and :erl_tar.extract({:binary, body}, [:memory, :compressed]) for application/gzip / .tgz. Each returns the full decompressed archive contents as a [{name, bytes}] list in memory, with no per-entry or total size cap. decompress_body/1 walks the content-encoding header and chains :zlib/:brotli/:ezstd decoders, so a response advertising content-encoding: gzip, gzip, gzip inflates through multiple layers without bound.
Both steps are enabled by default, no caller opt-in is required, and the attacker controls the content-type and content-encoding headers on their own server (or on any host reached via Req's automatic redirect following). A sub-megabyte response can expand to multiple gigabytes on the victim, crashing the BEAM process.
This issue affects req: from 0.1.0 before 0.6.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-49754 [CVSS:4.0 8.2 HIGH]
item.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-mint Mint allows attacker-controlled HTTP/2 servers to exhaust memory in a Mint client (HTTP/2 CONTINUATION flood).
When Mint's HTTP/2 receive path observes a HEADERS frame without the END_HEADERS flag, the unparsed header-block fragment is parked in conn.headers_being_processed, and every subsequent CONTINUATION frame on that stream is appended to the accumulator. Nothing in the receive path caps the accumulator: there is no per-stream size limit, no CONTINUATION frame-count limit, and max_header_list_size is only enforced on outgoing requests, never on inbound header blocks (its default is :infinity).
A malicious or compromised HTTP/2 server can stream an endless sequence of CONTINUATION frames (each up to the peer-advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE) and drive the client's iolist to arbitrary size, causing memory exhaustion and BEAM process death. A single connection to an attacker-controlled HTTP/2 endpoint is sufficient.

item.title: CVE-2026-49753 [CVSS:4.0 6.3 MEDIUM]
item.description:
Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling') vulnerability in elixir-mint Mint allows attacker-controlled HTTP/1 servers to desynchronise response framing on shared connections.
Mint's HTTP/1 Content-Length parser, Mint.HTTP1.Parse.content_length_header/1 in lib/mint/http1/parse.ex, parses the header value with Integer.parse/1, which accepts an optional + or - sign prefix. The length >= 0 guard rejects negatives, but inputs such as +0 or +123 are returned as valid lengths. RFC 7230 specifies Content-Length = 1*DIGIT, with no sign character permitted.
A fronting proxy or load balancer that strictly enforces the grammar will reject or reframe a header like Content-Length: +0, while Mint silently treats it as zero. When Mint reuses the socket (keep-alive, pipelining, or any pooled connection shared across requesters), the parser disagreement is a response-smuggling primitive: the proxy delimits the body one way, Mint another, and bytes from one response get attributed to the next. Where the same Mint connection is shared across trust boundaries, an attacker-controlled upstream can leak bytes into a different consumer's response stream.
This issue affects mint: from 0.1.0 before 1.9.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-48862 [CVSS:4.0 8.2 HIGH]
item.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-mint Mint allows attacker-controlled HTTP/2 servers to exhaust memory in a Mint client via PUSH_PROMISE flooding.
In lib/mint/http2.ex, Mint.HTTP2.decode_push_promise_headers_and_add_response/5 inserts a :reserved_remote entry into conn.streams for every promised stream ID. The neighbouring Mint.HTTP2.assert_valid_promised_stream_id/2 only verifies that the promised ID is even and not already present; client_settings.max_concurrent_streams is not consulted at promise time. The concurrency cap is only checked when the response HEADERS for the promised stream arrive, so a server that emits PUSH_PROMISE frames and withholds the matching HEADERS never trips that check.
HTTP/2 server push is accepted by default (client_settings.enable_push defaults to true). A single long-lived HTTP/2 connection to a hostile server lets that server pin one conn.streams entry per PUSH_PROMISE frame it sends, with no upper bound, until the client process runs out of memory.
This issue affects mint: from 0.2.0 before 1.9.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-48861 [CVSS:4.0 2.1 LOW]
item.description:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in elixir-mint Mint allows HTTP Request Splitting and HTTP Request Smuggling.
In lib/mint/http1/request.ex, the encode_request_line/2 function splices the caller-supplied method and target arguments directly into the HTTP/1 request line without any character validation: [method, ?\s, target, " HTTP/1.1\r\n"]. Mint 1.7.0 introduced validate_request_target/2, which rejects CRLF and other control characters in the target by default and closes the path/query vector unless the caller opts out via skip_target_validation: true. item.title: CVE-2026-47076 [CVSS:4.0 6.9 MEDIUM]
item.description:

hackney_url:normalize/2 URL-decodes the host component after the URL has been parsed into a #hackney_url{} record. item.title: CVE-2026-47073 [CVSS:4.0 8.7 HIGH]
item.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in benoitc hackney allows Flooding.
The WebSocket client in src/hackney_ws.erl imposes no upper bound on memory consumption in three code paths. First, read_handshake_response/3 accumulates received bytes into a growing buffer with no size cap; the per-receive timeout resets on every chunk, so a server that streams bytes without ever sending \r\n\r\n causes the buffer to grow until memory is exhausted. Second, parse_payload/9 and parse_active_payload/8 do not validate the declared frame payload length against any limit; because RFC 6455 allows payload lengths up to 2^63-1 bytes, a server that announces a very large frame and dribbles bytes causes the accumulation buffer to grow until OOM. Third, the frag_buffer field in #ws_data{} accumulates continuation frames indefinitely; a server that sends an endless stream of non-final (nofin) fragmented frames without ever sending a final (fin) frame grows frag_buffer without bound.
In all three cases the attacker only needs to control the WebSocket server the hackney client connects to, with no authentication or special client configuration required.
This issue affects hackney: from 2.0.0-beta.1 before 4.0.1.
